{{Short description|Scatterplot diagnostics measures}}
{{Expand language|name=Scagnostics|langcode=de|date=March 2022}}
[[File:ScagnosticsExampleSplom.svg|thumb|upright=2|Scatterplot matrix of the scagnostics measures for the 91 scatterplots of the variables of the Boston Housing data set]]
'''Scagnostics''' ('''sca'''tterplot dia'''gnostics''') is a series of measures that characterize certain properties of a point cloud in a [[scatter plot]]. The term and idea was coined by [[John Tukey]] and [[Paul Tukey]], though they didn't publish it; later it was elaborated by Wilkinson, Anand, and Grossman. The following nine dimensions are considered:<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wilkinson |first1=Leland |title=Scagnostics |date=23 April 2008 |url=https://escholarship.org/uc/item/9m31j1tb |access-date=25 March 2022 |language=en}}</ref><ref>{{cite book | last1=Wilkinson | first1=L. | last2=Anand | first2=A. | last3=Grossman | first3=R. | title=IEEE Symposium on Information Visualization, 2005. INFOVIS 2005 | chapter=Graph-theoretic scagnostics | date=2005 | pages=157–164 | doi=10.1109/INFVIS.2005.1532142 | isbn=0-7803-9464-X }}</ref>

# For the outliers in the data:
## outlying
# For the density of data points:
## skewed
## clumpy
## sparse
## striated
# For the shape of the point cloud:
## convex
## skinny
## stringy
# For trends in the data:
## monotony
